data.body:
`persisted_machine_id` (`src/machine.rs:45-52`) does an unsynchronized
read-derive-write, and `system_seed` (`src/machine.rs:86-93`) falls back to a
fresh random `Uuid::now_v7()` when neither `/etc/machine-id` nor
`/var/lib/dbus/machine-id` exists, which is the case on macOS and Windows.
`persist` (`src/machine.rs:95-100`) is a non-atomic `fs::write` whose error is
discarded.

Failure on macOS with a fresh store: `kno lease ls` (a read command that
resolves the machine id and takes no repo lock) runs concurrently with the
first `kno lease create`. Both find no `.knots/machine-id`, derive different
random-seeded digests A and B, and both write; last write wins. If the
lease-creating process derived B but A won the file, the lease is stamped with
owner B while every later local-lease query resolves A. `count_local_active_leases`
then returns 0 and sync proceeds unblocked while an agent on this machine
really does hold that lease -- the exact condition the guard exists to prevent.

The same disowning happens deterministically on macOS if `.knots/machine-id` is
ever deleted or the store rebuilt, because the value cannot be regenerated. On
Linux it regenerates identically from `/etc/machine-id`, so this is
platform-specific.

Scope:
- Make first-use persistence atomic: write to a temp file in the same
  directory and rename, or create-new and re-read the winner on `AlreadyExists`
  so every racer converges on the same id.
- Stop discarding the persist error; a machine id that fails to persist should
  surface, not silently re-randomize next call.
- Consider deriving a stable per-store seed on platforms with no system machine
  id, so a deleted `.knots/machine-id` is recoverable rather than a new
  identity.
data.title: Make first-use machine id persistence atomic
